g.text: KV Cache & Attention Variants — visual companion to Study notes → Deep-dive explanation
KV cache = trade GPU memory for compute. Variants shrink the memory; serving tricks move/manage it faster.
• Prefill: whole prompt in ONE parallel pass (compute-bound, sets TTFT)
• Decode: strictly sequential, 1 token per step (memory-bandwidth-bound, ~20–30 ms/token)
• Left-pad batches for generation so position -1 is a real token; mask PADs; position_ids = cumsum-1
• Special tokens: <BOS> start/attention sink, <EOS> stop, <PAD> masked, chat-template role tokens
2. Naive decoding vs KV cache — prefill & decode (A6–A8)
Naive (naive_decode.generate_naive): recompute K,V for ALL t tokens every step → Σt = O(T²)
• Cache K and V, NOT Q: Q is the current token's question; old K/V never change (causal)
• Per-step attention: 1 query × t keys = O(t); cache memory = O(T)
• mha.py: is_causal = past_kv is None (SDPA's causal mask is top-left aligned when q_len≠k_len)
• Decode latency ≳ (weight bytes + KV bytes) / HBM bandwidth → shrink bytes, not FLOPs
KV bytes = 2 (K,V) × L layers × H_kv heads × d_head × dtype_bytes × T seq_len × B batch
GPU memory ≈ weights + KV cache + activations/workspace + runtime overhead
→ at long context / high concurrency the KV cache, not the weights, caps how many users fit.
Note: session06 passes MLA through the ×2 (K+V) formula — MLA caches ONE latent, so true size is half.
• GQA dial: num_kv_groups = num_heads → MHA ; = 1 → MQA. Cache only G heads, repeat_interleave for math.
• MLA: cache a low-rank latent per token (independent of head count) + small decoupled RoPE key,
because rotation (position-dependent) can't be folded into the static up-projection.
• Production MLA 'absorbs' W_uk into W_q and W_uv into W_o → attention runs on the latent directly.
• RoPE (rope.py): rotate Q,K BEFORE caching; new token uses apply_rotary(offset=past_len).
Context extension: Position Interpolation → NTK-aware → YaRN (per-frequency ramp).
lessons/session01…10_*.py — rich-terminal presentation layer (imports the real modules, re-implements nothing)
• All variants share one interface: forward(x, past_kv) → (out, new_cache)
• Every module has a runnable _demo(); docs/ = MkDocs site, docs/assets/diagrams/ = 12 interactive HTML diagrams
• S10 PagedAttention = CPU allocation simulation; CUDA FlashAttention/vLLM benches referenced in colab/ (missing)
Naive: preallocate max_len contiguous per request → waste = max_len − actual
Paged: fixed 16-token blocks allocated on demand; waste ≤ block_size−1
Physical KV blocks in GPU HBM
P2 = shared prefix block (prefix caching / copy-on-write)
• Block table = logical → physical mapping per sequence (like OS virtual memory)
• Enables continuous batching: sequences join/leave every iteration, blocks freed & reused
• Prefix caching: vLLM hashes blocks (APC); SGLang RadixAttention uses a radix tree
• Kernel (FlashAttention/FlashInfer paged) reads K,V via the block table
7. SOTA inference routes — layer → bottleneck attacked (Part C2)
Architecture: GQA / MQA / MLA · sliding window · hybrid SSM · MoE
Quantisation: FP8/INT4/NVFP4 weights · FP8/INT4 KV cache
Decoding: speculative (draft, Medusa, EAGLE-3, MTP, n-gram)
Parallelism: TP · PP · EP · context parallel
System: disaggregated prefill/decode (Dynamo, llm-d) · KV-aware routing
Engines: vLLM · SGLang · TensorRT-LLM · llama.cpp/Ollama · TGI · LMDeploy
Metrics: TTFT (prefill) · TPOT/ITL (decode) · throughput · cost per 1M tokens
RL w/ verifiable reward: GRPO · DAPO
Quantise (FP8/INT4) → serve merged or multi-LoRA on vLLM / SGLang
LoRA on k/v_proj changes K,V → base-model prefix cache not reusable (aLoRA fixes this).
